summary:
The meeting covered personal development, business progress, and creative ambitions. Participants discussed managing responsibilities, building confidence, and moving ventures forward.

Anel reflected on time with her sick pet before his euthanasia and how her mother’s presence helped her accept the decision. David encouraged her to leave some newly available time unstructured. Jill explored whether her acting ambition was affecting business follow-through; David emphasized meeting present responsibilities while preserving room for creative pursuits.

Max said a commitment had improved business operations and team openness. The team was making progress on a financial challenge, described as roughly 40% through the solution and 20% toward payback. Max also reported greater confidence in making decisions without seeking as much approval.

Farrah and Charlie agreed on a purchase price for a business within 24 hours of their conversation. Choosing a trademarkable name and completing attorney paperwork remained unresolved. Farrah identified fear of mistakes as a source of hesitation and adopted the belief that mistakes are manageable and she is capable.

Carlos described business and work changes alongside a clearer vision following his 90-day plan. Chris reported growth in his peptide business, progress on his house, improved trust with Ronda, and changes in self-care and family interactions. Ronda said she felt safer as Chris became more aware of his anger and regulated his reactions; David emphasized that her sense of safety was her responsibility.

Erica presented a smart boxing bag with sensors, displays, smartphone connectivity, a camera, and training features. She had a U.S. patent and two trademarks, and the product was in the prototype phase with components ready for assembly.

Kimberly described her speaking and podcast goals, her story of moving from disconnection to self-worth, and her three pillars: reconnect, rewrite, and rebuild. She identified the audience outcome she wanted—her self-love spilling over to listeners—and committed to foregrounding that benefit when approaching podcasts.
